title: Signed repeated-grip change does not demonstrate incremental walking-disability discrimination across independently sampled NHANES cycles
abstract: Peak grip measures discard trial order. We tested signed first-to-third bilateral change, normalized by the sum of hand-specific maxima, against a strong baseline of demographics, BMI, combined peak strength, asymmetry, mean and unordered dispersion. Source-only ridge models used 1453 NHANES2011–12 adults aged60+ (277 reporting difficulty walking without special equipment); untouched2013–14 confirmation included1550 adults and300 cases. Source fivefold out-of-fold deltaAUC was−0.000657. Target baseline AUC0.742651 versus candidate0.739963 gave delta−0.002688 (2000 paired bootstrap95%CI−0.006396 to0.000819); Brier loss worsened by0.000377. Joint source/target refitting also included zero. The prespecified incremental-prediction criterion failed. This is a bounded negative result for this feature and fixed model, not evidence that repeated-grip dynamics never contain physiological information.
